Most homeowners call us after the third snake job in a year. If any of these sound familiar, a camera inspection will tell you what's actually happening underground.
Drains back up again weeks after clearing.
Toilets bubble when the tub drains.
A smell in the basement or the yard.
Lush strips of lawn over the line's path.
Roots pulled out on your plumber's snake.

Instead of digging a trench the full length of your sewer or water line, we open one or two small access points and repair or replace the pipe underground. Your lawn, driveway, trees and landscaping stay where they are.

There are two main ways to do it. Pipe lining builds a new pipe inside the old one. Pipe bursting pulls a brand-new pipe through while breaking the old one apart. The camera tells us which one you need.

It depends on the length of the line, how deep it is, how easy it is to reach, and whether it needs lining or bursting. After a camera inspection you get a written quote with a fixed scope, so there are no surprises.
Is a lined pipe as strong as a new one?
A cured-in-place liner forms a seamless, jointless pipe inside the old one. With no joints, roots have nowhere to get in. Design life and liner spec.
Will you have to dig at all?
Usually one or two small access points, not a trench. If the camera shows a sag or a section that's out of grade, digging that one spot may be the better fix, and we'll tell you before we start.
How long does the job take, and can I use my plumbing?
Most jobs take X day(s). Your water or sewer is off for hours, not days, and we'll tell you exactly when.
Can you fix a pipe full of tree roots?
Yes. We clear the roots, then line the pipe so there are no joints for them to grow back through.
What if my pipe has collapsed?
Lining needs a pipe that still holds its shape. For a collapsed or crushed line, pipe bursting pulls a brand-new HDPE pipe through the old path.
Do you work on commercial and industrial properties?
Yes. Along with homes, we repair and replace lines for commercial and industrial properties, and we choose methods that keep your property running during the work.
How do you decide which method to use?

We look at the pipe on camera, plus access points, soil, surface use and nearby utilities. Then we recommend the method that fits: bursting for full replacement, lining for sound host pipes, or a point repair when damage is isolated. You get the reasoning, schedule and budget in writing.
Does homeowners insurance cover sewer line repair?

settings.text: Fix a cracked, leaking or root-filled sewer line from the inside, without trenching your yard. We build a new, seamless pipe inside your old one through one or two small access points.

settings.altText: An old sewer pipe cut open, with the new blue liner cured inside it

Cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining is a trenchless sewer repair. A resin-saturated liner is pulled or inverted into the cleaned host pipe, inflated against the walls and cured until it hardens into a jointless new pipe. Most residential jobs need little or no digging.

How long does a lined pipe last?

Can roots grow through a liner?

Will lining make my pipe smaller?

Can you line a pipe that has a belly in it?

pages.title: Pipe Bursting
pages.excerpt: Trenchless pipe bursting in Spokane: replace a collapsed, crushed or undersized sewer line with new seamless HDPE pipe through two small access pits.

settings.text: Replace a collapsed, crushed or undersized sewer line without trenching your yard. A bursting head breaks the old pipe apart underground while a brand-new HDPE pipe is pulled in right behind it, through two small access pits.
See if bursting fits your line
Written & reviewed by Mike Jeisma, owner, 14+ years in trenchless repair · Updated Month YYYY

settings.altText: A shored access pit in a front lawn, with the camera reel and jetter beside it

settings.text: One of the small access pits: shored, with the camera and jetter on hand.

Pipe bursting is a trenchless way to replace a sewer line. A cone-shaped bursting head is pulled through the old pipe from one access pit to another. It breaks the old pipe outward into the soil, and a new, seamless HDPE pipe follows behind it in the same path. You end up with a completely new pipe, and it can be a size larger than the old one.
Is bursting right for your pipe?
When bursting works, and when it doesn't.
Bursting replaces the whole run between two pits, so it shines when the old pipe is past saving. The camera shows which fix fits, and we'll show you the footage either way.
Clay pipe that's broken or badly offset
Pipe too small for the household (upsize)
Long runs under lawns, driveways and landscaping
Pipe still round, with cracks or roots
Line under a slab or inside the house
One damaged spot on a good line

settings.text: Trenchless water line pulling in Spokane
Replace an old, leaking or corroded water service line without trenching your yard. We pull a new CTS poly line underground, reconnect it, and test it for pressure and leaks.
Written & reviewed by Mike Jeisma, owner, 14+ years in sewer & water line work · Updated Month YYYY

settings.altText: Access pit with the new blue water line in place next to the meter box

settings.text: A small access pit at the meter, with the new line pulled in.

Water line pulling is a trenchless way to replace the water service line that feeds your home. Instead of digging a trench the whole length of the line, we open small access pits and pull a new CTS poly line underground. Then we reconnect it and test it for pressure and leaks. The new line doesn't rust or build up scale, so you get your water pressure back.
CTS poly, no rust or scale

It's polyethylene water pipe made to copper tube size (CTS), so it connects to standard fittings. It doesn't rust or build up scale inside like old galvanized pipe does.
Will a new line fix my low water pressure?
If the pressure is lost in a corroded or leaking service line, yes. If the cause is the city main or your house plumbing, a new line won't fix it, and we'll tell you before you spend the money.

pages.excerpt: Sewer point repairs in Spokane: when the damage is in one spot, we reline just that section from inside the pipe instead of replacing the whole line.

settings.text: When the damage is isolated to one section and the rest of the pipe is sound, we reline just that spot instead of replacing the whole line. One crack, one bad joint, one root problem: fixed from inside the pipe.
See if a spot fix will do
Written & reviewed by Mike Jeisma, owner, 14+ years in trenchless repair · Updated Month YYYY
Illustration: a spot liner sealing one damaged section, with the sound pipe on either side left as it is.

A point repair fixes one damaged section of a sewer line from the inside. The camera finds the exact spot, then a short liner is carried to it on an inflatable packer, pressed against the old pipe and left to cure. The result is a sealed, jointless patch over the damage, while the rest of the line, which is still sound, stays as it is.
Is a point repair right for your pipe?
When one fix is enough, and when it isn't.
A point repair only makes sense if the rest of the line is in good shape. The camera shows us the whole pipe, and we'll show you the footage either way.

Is a point repair a permanent fix?

For the spot it covers, yes: the patch seals the damage with a jointless liner. It doesn't fix the rest of the line, which is why we check the whole pipe on camera first. Expected life and PNW warranty terms.
Why not just line the whole pipe?
If the rest of the line is sound, you don't need to pay for it. If the camera shows damage in several places, we'll tell you, and lining the whole run may be the better deal.
Usually not. The patch goes in through a cleanout. When a small access point is needed.

Will roots come back at that joint?
The patch covers the joint the roots got in through, so there's no gap left at that spot. Mike's experience with roots at other joints.
Can you fix more than one spot?
Yes, each damaged spot can get its own patch. Past X spots, lining the whole line often costs about the same, and we'll show you both options.
